links.note: Was on 32886 Villages to Cities, which covers the geography and the naming and says nothing about layout. The larger Harappan cities being built according to precise plans, with wide streets oriented to the cardinal directions, is stated in 32888, the town-planning concept.

Was on 32886 Villages to Cities. The two distinct parts of a Harappan settlement, an upper town for the elite and a lower town for common people, are set out in 32888; Dholavira's three zones in 32889 are the stated exception the item's third option plays on.

Was on 32886 Villages to Cities, which has nothing on building material. 32888 is the construction concept - individual houses of various sizes lining the streets and lanes, with the quality of construction the same for small and big houses - and it is against its brick norm that Dholavira's stone foundations are called exceptional.

Was on 32886 Villages to Cities. A fortification is glossed as a massive wall surrounding a settlement, generally for protective purposes, in 32888, in the same sentence that says most Harappan cities had one.

Was on 32896 The Lothal Pot and the Bangles, which is about the story painted on a pot from Lothal, not the settlement's structure. Lothal's surprisingly huge basin, 214 by 36 metres, and the inference that it must have been a dockyard, are in 32894.

Was on 32893 Exports, Carnelian and Bronze, matched on the word bronze figurine. The Dancing Girl is discussed only in 32896, where the LET'S EXPLORE asks what attitude the figurine expresses and to observe her bangles covering an entire arm.

Was on 32886 Villages to Cities, which is about the rise of the cities rather than their end. The item turns on invasion being ruled out, and 32897 is the concept that says there is no trace of warfare or invasion and that the Harappans seem to have kept no army or weapons of war.
Was on 32886 Villages to Cities. The contrast between the upper town where the local elite probably lived and the lower town where common people lived is stated in 32888.
Was on 32886 Villages to Cities. Large buildings that seem to have been used for collective purposes, for instance warehouses, appear in 32888 among the features of the planned cities.

Was on 32886 Villages to Cities, the rise rather than the aftermath. The statement that although the cities disappeared much of the Harappan culture and technology survived and was passed on to the next phase of Indian civilisation sits in 32898, and continuity of traditions is exactly that claim.
